newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker amid new supply.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker amid new supply.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, underperforming U.S. treasuries as a wave of provincial government and corporate supply weighed on the market, analysts said.

"It was supply oriented. But even though we had a lot of supply today and we're being faced with supply next week, the market seems fairly orderly," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.55 to C$111.45 to yield 7.035 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.99 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to five basis points from an all-time low of three basis points on Wednesday.

The Canadian bond market weakened as C$1.0 billion in new supply arrived on the market during the session. Half that came from the Province of Quebec, which set C$150 million of 10-year bonds and C$350 million of 30-year bonds on financial markets. The bonds were reopenings of a previous issues.
The Royal Bank of Canada, the country's largest bank, also set C$500 million in subordinated debentures on financial markets during the session.

The Bank of Canada also released details of the Government of Canada's auction of five-year bonds on May 28. The Canadian government will sell a total C$2.6 billion of bonds with a coupon of 5.5 percent and maturing on September 1, 2002.
The Bank of Canada will buy a minimum of C$390 million of the new bonds.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.38 to C$103.50 to yield 6.501 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 28 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.92 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.18 percent.
